To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ester and cyclopropyl analogs of succinic semiaaldehyde are substrates for the enzyme succinate semialdehdye dehydrogenase.
the carboxylic group of SSA is involved in the process of substrate inhibition and that the enzyme has a preference for the transoid conformation of the substrate.
the carboxymethyl ester of SSA is a substrate for SSADH and that the trans‐1‐ formyl‐cycopropan‐2‐ carboxylic acid, an analogue of SSA, inhibits SSADH in the same concentration range as SSA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the mechanism of the inhibition of SSADHS by SSA, and the results obtained suggest that the enzyme is a good candidate for the study of the mechanism.
studies on analogues of succinic semaldehyde (SSA), which is the immediate metabolite of γ‐aminobubyric acid in the catabolic pathway.
the conformational properties of the substrate of SSADH and their influence on enzyme activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SSA is not essential for the inhibition of SSADHS by SSA.
the carboxylic acid moiety of the substrate is not directly involved in the inhibition of the enzyme by its substrate, but that the carboxamide group is essential for the inhibition process.
SSA and γ‐aminobutryric acid are present in a transoid conformation when bound to SSADH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the enzyme is able to accept as a substrate any carboxylic group that can be accommodated within the active site in a transoid configuration.
the carboxylic group of SSA is essential for the binding to the enzyme but not for its oxidation.
SSA, in its transoid form, can be considered as the substrate of SSADH, and that the enzyme‐substrate complex is stabilized by the interaction of the γ‐carboxylate group with the enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carboxylic group of SSA is essential in its function as substrate and inhibitor of the enzyme.
, in addition to γ‐aminobutanoic acid, succinic semialdehydes are also substrates of SS‐DH.
SSA‐Me is a useful substrate for SSADH.
